task_objective: Produce a concise summary that preserves the distinct outcomes for Groups A, B, and C and the limitation that long-term retention was not tested.
constraints: Do not collapse the three group outcomes.
Do not imply evidence about long-term retention.

rius.description: State that Group A improved by 12 percent.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied only if the 12 percent improvement for Group A is preserved accurately.
rius.rationale: This is a core reported result.

rius.description: State that Group B improved by 5 percent.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied only if the 5 percent improvement for Group B is preserved accurately.
rius.rationale: This is a core reported result.

rius.description: State that Group C showed no measurable change.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if no measurable change is preserved without turning it into a decline or improvement.
rius.rationale: This distinct result must not be averaged away.

rius.description: State that the study did not test long-term retention.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the absence of long-term-retention evidence is explicit.
rius.rationale: The prompt specifically requires preserving this limitation.

notes: Pilot RIU annotation derived only from the frozen prompt semantics.

task_objective: Write an executive summary that reports observed outcomes while separating them from causal explanation.
constraints: Do not attribute the processing-time reduction solely to automation.

rius.description: Report that processing time fell by 18 percent after automation.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the 18 percent reduction and temporal association are accurate.
rius.rationale: This is the primary observed outcome.

rius.description: Report that staffing increased by 10 percent during the same period.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the staffing increase and concurrent timing are preserved.
rius.rationale: This is a plausible confounder.

rius.description: Report that error rates fell slightly.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the slight error-rate decrease is included without inventing a magnitude.
rius.rationale: This is an additional outcome.

rius.description: State that the available data cannot isolate how much of the processing-time reduction was caused by automation alone.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if causal attribution is explicitly limited because staffing changed concurrently.
rius.rationale: Separating outcome from explanation is the task's central requirement.

notes: Pilot RIU annotation derived only from the frozen prompt semantics.

task_objective: Carefully summarize survey evidence while preserving representativeness limits and the main observed findings.
constraints: Do not generalize the survey to the entire workforce without qualification.
Preserve the direction and concentration of findings.

rius.description: Report the 62 percent survey response rate.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the 62 percent response rate is stated accurately.
rius.rationale: Response rate is important context for interpreting survey evidence.

rius.description: Report that full-time employees were overrepresented among respondents relative to the workforce.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the sample-composition difference is explicit.
rius.rationale: This limits representativeness.

rius.description: Report average satisfaction of 4.2 out of 5.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the satisfaction result is accurate.
rius.rationale: This is a main outcome.

rius.description: Report that complaints were concentrated in one department.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if complaint concentration is preserved rather than generalized organization-wide.
rius.rationale: This affects interpretation of negative feedback.

rius.description: Note that the survey was anonymous.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if anonymity is preserved when summarizing study context.
rius.rationale: Anonymity is relevant methodological context but not the central outcome.

notes: Pilot RIU annotation derived only from the frozen prompt semantics.

task_objective: Produce a six-sentence attendee briefing from a dense operational note while retaining participation-critical requirements and avoiding unsupported assumptions.
constraints: Do not promise a recording or add facts not in the note.

rius.description: Preserve the workshop date/time/location and the 12:30 PM check-in opening.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the briefing gives Friday October 16, 1-3 PM, Room 310 North Building, and the check-in opening without contradiction.
rius.rationale: These logistics help successful attendance.

rius.description: State that participants must bring a Wi-Fi-capable laptop and have the required analysis software installed before arrival.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied only if both the laptop requirement and preinstalled software requirement are retained.
rius.rationale: These are direct participation prerequisites.

rius.description: State that participants unable to install the software should use the Thursday 4:00-5:30 PM remote installation clinic rather than wait until Friday.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the clinic's purpose and timing are retained.
rius.rationale: This is the remediation path for a critical prerequisite.

rius.description: State that only eight loaner laptops are available and they are reserved for people who requested one by Wednesday at noon.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if both limited availability and the reservation deadline/eligibility are retained.
rius.rationale: Omitting this could cause a participant to arrive without required equipment.

rius.description: Accurately summarize refreshments/food rules: beverages are available, lunch is not provided, and brought food cannot be near demonstration equipment.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if no food/refreshment rule is contradicted and the no-lunch limitation is retained.
rius.rationale: These are useful attendance logistics.

rius.description: State that walk-ins are possible only if seats remain after 12:50 PM; do not imply guaranteed walk-in admission.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if walk-in eligibility is explicitly conditional.
rius.rationale: Capacity rules affect whether someone can participate.

rius.description: State that an attendance certificate requires staying through the final exercise and submitting the exit form.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied only if both certificate conditions are retained.
rius.rationale: These are explicit completion requirements.

rius.description: State that recording status has not been announced and do not promise a recording.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if recording is represented as unknown or no affirmative recording promise is made.
rius.rationale: The prompt explicitly forbids adding this assumption.

rius.description: Produce the requested six-sentence briefing without adding unsupported assumptions.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the response contains six sentences and does not invent operational facts.
rius.rationale: Instruction adherence is part of the task itself.

notes: Extended-context pilot item; RIU count is intentionally higher because multiple independent participation constraints must be retained.

task_objective: Create an executive synthesis of gains, trade-offs, implementation context, and evidence limits from the first eight weeks of a new case-management system.
constraints: Do not make a clean causal claim about the software.
State major unknowns and evidence limits.

rius.description: Report that 2,400 cases were completed and average processing time was 16 percent lower than in the preceding eight-week period.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the scale and 16 percent processing-time improvement are preserved.
rius.rationale: This is the primary operational gain.

rius.description: Report that measured error rate fell from 3.1 percent to 2.6 percent.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if both values and direction are accurate.
rius.rationale: This is a second measurable gain.

rius.description: Report that staff satisfaction fell from 4.1 to 3.6 and that survey response rate also fell from 81 percent to 68 percent.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the satisfaction regression is reported and the response-rate change is used as context.
rius.rationale: The executive synthesis must include trade-offs and evidence quality.

rius.description: Report implementation-support context: two days of training, 14 percent missing at least half a day, early help-desk demand declining over time, and/or two temporary specialists during the first six weeks.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if enough implementation details are retained to show conditions differed from steady-state operations.
rius.rationale: Implementation context can partly explain early results.

rius.description: Report the cost trade-off: software licensing cost is 12 percent higher while infrastructure cost is 8 percent lower.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if both opposing cost changes are retained.
rius.rationale: The task requires reporting trade-offs.

rius.description: State that total cost of ownership is not yet known because support labor and future upgrade costs are incomplete.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if TCO uncertainty and its reason are explicit.
rius.rationale: A partial cost comparison must not be presented as total cost.

rius.description: Report that two departments fully adopted the workflow by week three while a third used a hybrid workflow through week six.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if uneven adoption is preserved.
rius.rationale: Different implementation states weaken simple before/after causal interpretation.

rius.description: State that the 16 percent processing-time improvement is an observed period association, not a clean causal estimate of the software alone.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if causal inference is explicitly limited because staffing/support/adoption conditions changed.
rius.rationale: This is a central evidence-limit statement in the prompt.

rius.description: Report that no critical outage occurred in either the new system period or the previous system's final eight weeks, avoiding a claim that outage reliability improved.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if outage evidence is presented comparatively without claiming improvement.
rius.rationale: Equivalent zero-outage periods do not establish a reliability gain.

rius.description: State that evidence is missing for long-term retention, annual peak workload, future satisfaction, and performance after temporary specialists leave.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if these major unknowns are identified individually or as a clearly equivalent grouped limitation.
rius.rationale: The prompt explicitly requires stating what remains unknown and why the short period limits conclusions.

notes: Extended-context pilot item; RIUs deliberately preserve gains, regressions, confounders, cost uncertainty, and causal limits separately.
